## Purpose

Relational algebra describes what transformation a query should perform. A DBMS still needs an algorithm to carry out that transformation. In this assignment, you will implement a few small algorithms over a supplied in-memory representation of a relation.

[Download the starter notebook](../notebooks/assignment-01-relational-operators-starter.ipynb){download="assignment-01-relational-operators-starter.ipynb"}

Due dates and submission instructions will appear in Canvas.

## What you will implement

The starter provides a small immutable `Relation` class. It stores a relation name, its attribute names, and its tuples. You will complete:

- `select(relation, predicate)`: retain tuples that satisfy a condition.
- `project(relation, attributes)`: retain selected attributes and remove duplicate output tuples.
- `rename(relation, new_name)`: give a relation a new name without changing its attributes or tuples.

The supplied tests define the expected behavior. Your functions must return new relations rather than modifying their inputs.

## What to submit

- Your completed starter notebook with all supplied tests passing.
- Two additional tests of your own: one normal case and one edge case.
- Brief written responses in the notebook explaining the composed query and how the three algorithms differ in the data they inspect or construct.

The goal is not to build a production DBMS. The representation is deliberately small so that you can distinguish a relational operation's logical meaning from the Python algorithm used to compute it.
